block-definition.comment: Dictionary maker! To use, expand the inputs and drag the (key: [] value: []) blocks into the slots for each k/v pair.
Represents one key-value pair, you can use it in the dictionary constructor block, but also in append blocks and stuff
A nicer dictionary constructor. To use, just click the arrows and input the key/value pairs (no k/v block required!)
Get a value or index of a key in a dictionary.
Get a list of only the keys or values of an array (entries option isn't included, since the dictionary itself is already stored as a list of entries)

Reporter version of the "add [thing] to list" block, operates on a list then returns the result of the operation. (This block doesn't exist for dictionaries since you can just drag a "key: value:" block to the "thing" input.)
Reporter version of the "delete (1) of list" block, operates on a list then returns the result of the operation.
Reporter version of the "insert [thing] at (1) of list" block, operates on a list then returns the result of the operation.
Reporter version of the "replace item (1) of list with [thing]" block, operates on a list then returns the result of the operation.
Check if a dictionary contains a given key.
Iterate over each key/value pair of a dictionary.
Delete a key of a dictionary and report the result.
Get the value of a variable by its name.
Set the value of a variable by its name.
Put a variable (selected by its name) through a function and sets that variable to the return value of the function.
A multiline string literal (just reports its input) not sure if this is useful at all and even if it is you could just use other blocks but whatever

Switch case statement! Get the value of the reporter after the "switch", and do something if it's one of the values after the "case"s. If it isn't, it will default to the function under the "default".
Reporter version of the switch-case block. Instead of running a function, it reports the value in the given case.

block-definition.s: replace item %'item' of %'list' with %'val or kv?' %'thing'
block-definition.comment: Replace a key of a dictionary with either a new value (keep old key), new key (keep old value), or a key/value pair, and report the result.
Reports the value Infinity. this is also probably not useful at all
Replace every occurence of a substring in a given string and replace it with a new string.
Get a substring (range of characters) from a string. NOTE: If you want a "sublist of list" block, then use the "item (1) of list" block with a range as the items to select.
Repeat a string the specified amount of times, and report the resulting string.
Calls a function on a certain value, repeating the call a certain amount of times.
Calls a function on a certain value, repeating the call until or while the result meets a certain condition.
Rounds a number to the nearest multiple of another number.
Get a list of factors (divisors) of the given number. NOTE: Using this block with 0 errors, as 0 has an infinite amount of factors (divisors).
Replace every occurence of a sublist in a given list and replace it with a new sublist.
Reports a range, starting with the specified number, with the specified amount of elements. Negative numbers make it go backwards.

block-definition.s: keep every %'n' th item from %'list' $nl offset %'offset'
block-definition.comment: Keep every n-th item from a list. "offset" is the number it starts counting at (minus 1).
Repeat the items of a list the specified amount of times, and report the resulting list.

Repeats each item of the first list by its corresponding item in the second list. If the second list is a scalar, or it's too short, it will be repeated for the entire length of the list. NOTE: I am thinking of implementing fill values eventually but idk if i could implement it
Gets either the greatest common divisor or the least common multiple of two numbers.
Throws an error with a specifed message.
Checks a boolean value. If it is true, it does nothing. If it is false, it will error, with an optional message specified (click the right arrow to set it.)
Throws an error with a specifed message.

Similar to the assert block, but as a reporter instead. Checks a boolean value. If it is true, it reports the input boolean. If it is false, it will error, with an optional message specified (click the right arrow to set it.)

Run the function inside with access to a "current value" var, then report the value of the "current value" var after running the function. NOTE: To make it work, you'll have to put a "set [current value v] to (value)" block at the start so it will be able to do calculations on it.
Comment block, used for putting remarks/notes in your code (but by itself does absolutely nothing)
Create a new vector from a given x and y coordinate. Fun fact: Vectors can be used in blocks like the "go to ()" and "distance to ()" blocks.

Tries the code inside the first script input. If it doesn't error, do nothing. If it does error, run the code inside the second script input, with access to an "error" variable that holds the string contents of the error.

Tries reporting the code inside the first text input. If it doesn't error, do nothing. If it does error, report the code inside the second text input, with access to an "error" variable that holds the string contents of the error.

Tries running the code inside the first command input. If it doesn't error, do nothing. If it does error, report the code inside the second text input, with access to an "error" variable that holds the string contents of the error.
Tries reporting the code inside the first text input, and reports if it errored.
Tries running the code inside the first command input, and reports if it errored.

Flatten a nested list, with a specified depth to start flattening the nested lists from. NOTE: If you need to flatten a list so it fully becomes a list, without any other lists as elements, use the "flatten" option in the "[length v] of list" block.
Create a new vector from a given magnitude (length) and angle.
Gets a certain vector constant. - zero (origin) = [0, 0] - one = [1, 1] - infinity = [Infinity, Infinity] - left = [-1, 0] - up = [0, 1] - right = [1, 0] - down = [0, -1]

inputs.input: zero (origin)zero (origin) one infinity ~ left right up down

block-definition.comment: Get the x, y, angle, magnitude, or normalized version of a vector. - x: The x component of the vector. - y: The y component of the vector. - angle: The angle the vector faces in. - magnitude: The length of the vector. - normalized: The vector divided by its magnitude, turns any vector into a unit vector with the same angle.
Rotate a given vector by the specified amount of degrees.

Apply a set operation (union, intersection, difference, symmetric difference) to two lists. - union: Items that appear in all of the lists, without duplicates. - intersection: Only items that appear in exactly two of the lists. - difference: Only items that appear in list A, but not also appear in list B. - symm. difference: Only items that appear in exactly one of the lists. P.S. the code for this block is absolutely awful so yea
Like the "[distance v] to [mouse-pointer v]" block, but can check from any position to any position. NOTE: The way this block works might be a bit slow and fragile, so uh yea
Compute the dot product of two vectors. The dot product of two vectors A and B is defined as A.x*B.x + A.y*B.y.
